structured.answer: If I have to pick from this page, I'd go with Harel, the "כספי (שקלי)" track: it's a name I know, it shows 0% in shares, and the fee is 0.57%. But I'm not putting in a shekel until I ask you or the bank what "כספי" means and whether it's really as safe as my deposit.

stuck.where: Screen 1, the buttons under 'במה הכסף מושקע'
stuck.why: Twenty buttons. 'עוקב מדד S&P 500', 'גמיש', 'סחיר', 'משולב'. I couldn't see which one means 'safe like a deposit'. Nothing there says 'safe' or 'deposit'.
Every row has six or seven numbers and a little coloured circle. I couldn't tell the two colours (green and yellow) apart well, and I didn't know what to look at first.
I didn't understand if that's a return or a warning. Most of Harel's rows have no number there at all.
I don't know what 'מט"ח' is, and in some rows it says 99% shares and 99% מט"ח. How can that make 198%? And one row at Meitav says '101%' shares.

findings.what: Nothing says which tracks are safe or can lose money. Someone like me can't tell 'כספי' or 'אג"ח סחיר' apart from a gamble.
findings.where: Filter buttons and the table, screens 1–5
Screen 1 filter buttons and many rows
findings.what: English letters 'S&P 500' right on the first screen made me feel this isn't for me.
A dark background with grey and thin text is hard on my eyes even with glasses. The column headings and the line under the title are especially pale.
Too many numbers in every row: two fees, two returns, two exposures, money managed. It made me anxious.
I can't tell the green and yellow circles apart, and nothing in words says what they mean.
'פחות מ־3 שנים' appears where I expected a number. I didn't know if it was bad.
The percentages for 3 and 5 years. Is that per year or in total? '3 שנים 24.04%' looks enormous, and I don't trust it.
Two management fees, 'מהחיסכון' and 'מההפקדות', and no plain explanation of which one I pay or what it means in shekels.
Shares and מט"ח percentages that add up to over 100%, even 101% shares. Confusing.
The page is very long, with 143 tracks. I stopped after five screens.
